articles.title: El Barcelona, bajo mínimos atrás
articles.standfirst: Koundé, Eric García y Christensen no estarán contra el PSG
articles.summary: Koundé, Eric García y Christensen no estarán contra el PSG
articles.body: El Barcelona afronta el compromiso del martes contra el PSG con un margen de recuperación mínimo y numerosas bajas en su línea defensiva. Hasta tres zagueros no viajarán este lunes a París: Koundé, Eric García y Christensen, todos ellos lesionados. Además, Gerard Martín arrastra un golpe, aunque no debería tener problemas para jugar. La expedición azulgrana se desplazará este lunes a la capital francesa con solo cinco defensas del primer equipo: Cancelo, Espart, Cubarsí, Gerard Martín y Balde. No obstante, este último apenas ha entrado en los planes de Hansi Flick, ya que solo ha disputado 12 minutos en lo que va de temporada, contra el Racing de Santander. En el caso de Gerard Martín, tuvo que ser sustituido al descanso del partido contra el Betis. El defensa recibió un pisotón que le obligó a permanecer varios minutos en la banda mientras era atendido por los servicios médicos. En principio, está disponible para el encuentro contra el PSG, pero solo dispone de dos días para recuperarse por completo y poder afrontar con plenas garantías una cita tan exigente. Con Koundé, Eric García y Christensen fuera de la convocatoria, Hansi Flick deberá reorganizar su línea defensiva. En los laterales, Cancelo podría ocupar la banda derecha, mientras que Xavi Espart apunta a la izquierda, después de firmar muy buenas actuaciones. En el centro de la zaga, Cubarsí está al cien por cien y la principal incógnita es quién será su acompañante. Si Gerard Martín está completamente recuperado de sus molestias en el tobillo, formará pareja con el central catalán, como es habitual. Si Gerard no acaba de tener buenas sensaciones, el técnico deberá buscar alternativas más imaginativas o recurrir a La Masía. De Jong sería la opción más natural, pero el neerlandés recibió el alta médica el viernes tras lesionarse durante el Mundial y no disputó ni un minuto contra el Betis. Por lo tanto, está sin ritmo de competición. Rodri también ocupó el eje de la zaga cuando Eric García abandonó el terreno de juego en La Cartuja, pero Flick no renunciará del internacional en el centro del campo. Con este panorama, el técnico cruza los dedos para que Gerard Martín llegue al cien por cien.

articles.title: Patrick Mahomes Shares Positive Update on Knee After Week 6 Win
articles.summary: Kansas City Chiefs quarterback Patrick Mahomes gave an update on state of his knee after the team's win against the Los Angeles Chargers. The post Patrick Ma...
articles.body:
The Kansas City Chiefs remain undefeated in the 2026 season, having beaten the Los Angeles Chargers in Week 6 to go 5-0.

The Chiefs are the only unbeaten team in the AFC, alongside the San Francisco 49ers and Minnesota Vikings make up the only teams to have not been bested yet in the NFL.

Perhaps the even more impressive note to the Chiefs' win-streak is the fact that quarterback Patrick Mahomes is coming off a serious knee injury back in December that saw him tear his ACL and LCL in his left knee.

Patrick Mahomes Speaks on Knee Health After Chargers Win

Mahomes was ready to start the year after making a quicker-than-expected recovery, and five games in has looked his best self in the regular season in almost half a decade.

Speaking to the media after the win against the Chargers, the former two-time MVP shared how his knee was feeling as he continues to get closer to 100%.

"After the bye week, I felt better physically… There's still some burst I don't have… But that's something we'll continue to work on." Mahomes said after the game, via Charles Goldman.

Patrick Mahomes 'Better' Despite Not Having Full Burst

Even though the 31-year old has been practicing since training camp and has yet to miss a game this season, his words make it clear that being on the field does not inherently imply a full bill of health in the National Football League.

The exact timeline for Mahomes getting his burst back to what it was prior to the injury is unknown. And for players sustaining serious knee injuries after the age of 30, there is no guarantee he'll ever be quite as fast as he was before.

But him feeling improved and is certainly a positive for the team, and whilst Mahomes is an agile QB, him having game-breaking speed has never been major part of his game.

articles.title: ‘The Gap’ in the WSL remains – but creating competition takes time
articles.summary: Good news first: it’s definitely shrinking. It being ‘The Gap’. The Gap being the space between the Women’s Super League’s entrenched top three and the rest....
articles.body:
Good news first: it's definitely shrinking. It being 'The Gap'. The Gap being the space between the Women's Super League's entrenched top three and the rest.

It is, though, assailable by pre-match face painting and savvy coaching and, if you're Birmingham City, who snagged a point off Arsenal on Saturday, Oceane Hurtre's left foot.

Of course, The Gap is still there if you're, say, Tottenham Hotspur or Brighton & Hove Albion, the former having suffered a 6-2 defeat to Chelsea before the latter fell 3-2 to Manchester City.

The result leaves Spurs with just two wins from 54 matches played against the WSL's top four (Chelsea, City, Arsenal and Manchester United), Chelsea claiming 13 wins from 13. While Brighton can boast two wins from their 13 meetings with City, Sunday was not one.

"After the first three goals, it was a bit like, 'Wow, are we that good and they are that bad?'" said City head coach Andree Jeglertz after his side's 3-2 victory. "Of course that's not the reality. If you drop a couple of percentages in this league, teams are good enough to punish you. Brighton is this type."

Jeglertz knows this. Brighton were one of only three teams to beat City last season to make their inevitable WSL title lift feel, for a brief moment, not so inevitable. Of course, City still lifted the trophy, handed Brighton a 4-0 defeat in the FA Cup final a month later and walked away Sunday with all three points as Brighton slumped to 10th.

But it's time for one of WSL's annual rituals: arguing whether this is the most competitive season to date, whether our collective patience and relentless hounding of head coaches regarding The Gap's existence and their plan to conquer it has finally coalesced into its closing.

Since the 2014-15 season — when Liverpool clinched the title ahead of Chelsea and Birmingham City finished third — the triumvirate of Chelsea, Arsenal and City have occupied the top three spots on all but two occasions, when Manchester United crashed in at second and third in the 2022-23 and 2024-25 seasons respectively.

This does nothing to blunt our enthusiasm each season, firing questions about The Gap like fevered confetti at those teams squatting on its wrong end. What's the plan this time, guys? Have you considered trying a pre-match DJ? Manchester City have a pre-match DJ. And £1.6million per year to pay Khadija 'Bunny' Shaw, who scored twice against Brighton.

Chelsea have eight league titles, a wage bill of nearly £15m as of 2024-25 and Lauren James, who also scored twice on Sunday. Arsenal do bottomless brunch. They also have decades' worth of infrastructure and history, plus women's football's first £1m player. Not their fault you don't, of course. But do you do bottomless brunch?

"Look, they didn't build what they've built in 15 months," head coach Martin Ho said ahead of the trip to Chelsea. "We'll get there, but we have years of work to do."

What Ho said is important. It's also important what he didn't say, the unenchanting euphemism skulking in the corner. "But you can't say that," one WSL executive, speaking anonymously to protect relationships, tells The Athletic .

"That" is the years of investment that women's teams are expected to make up in a matter of seasons, by ingenuity and passionate partnerships and letting fans take pints to their seats and appointing managers like Ho. Or, if you're London City Lionesses who currently sit third in the WSL table after their 2-1 win against Everton, hiring a matchday brass band. Plus spending at least £2.4million on transfer fees across two seasons and recruiting four players in the summer with nine Ballon d'Or Feminin nominations between them, including two-time winner Alexia Putellas.

This isn't some grim requiem for the game. It's not even a critique. Rather, it's the uncomfortable but necessary starting point for any conversation about The Gap.

This season has cut a compelling argument for its shrinking. According to Opta, non-big four sides averaged 0.42 points per game against the traditional big four before this weekend, the highest on record across a season since 2015 (0.43). This is in line with steady and increased investment by all clubs, almost all of which have broken their record transfer fees in the space of 18 months.

Yet, context is important. Arsenal are unexpectedly suffering their worst-ever start to a WSL season . United's jagged start boiled down to the appointment of a new manager just two weeks before the season's start. Hurtre's goal against Arsenal, coupled with one in the 3-1 defeat to Manchester City last month, represented the first time in WSL history that a promoted side scored against either team at first attempt, a reminder of just how gargantuan the gap was to begin with and remains. In the season's sixth week of fixtures, United, City, Chelsea and London City all comfortably saw off opposition by an aggregate score of 14-6.

That women's football harbours a deep desire to close The Gap isn't unique. This is the preoccupation of competitive sport, if not modern existence. How much bootstrap pulling is required here? What optimisations have we not considered?

At which point we should cast our eyes to the league next door, the one swamped in its own financial ruin, wondering who has the hose. Yes, we're talking about Manchester City's men's team, but all the rest of it too: the 94 per cent of men's clubs that lost money last season, the nearly two-thirds of English Football League and National League clubs that are technically insolvent , the more than a quarter in the top five divisions that would run out of cash within the lifespan of a fruit fly if their owners pulled the plug.

This should be a neon red sign for women's football. Almost all WSL sides remain financially dependent on their parent company, according to last season's financial records. Yet, salaries and transfer fees continue to fatten, despite revenue and attendances failing to keep up. Many clubs could be at risk of contravening the league's new financial rules come season's end.

Clubs investing seriously in their women's and girls' setups should be encouraged. The evidence is the fact that with each season, we ask about The Gap, more galvanised as the inches chip away.

Yet elite sport is inherently stratified. While breaking through is the thrill, we should be wary of cajoling teams to bridge the gap too quickly, to manoeuvre in manners that are unsustainable, that mimic mistakes elsewhere.

"The scoreline is obviously damaging," Ho said post-match. "But if you'd asked me whether we could push Chelsea as much as we did in that first 60 minutes, compared to 15 or 16 months ago, people would've probably said no."

articles.title: Combined match review: RSL earns second road victory of, Royals fall at home
articles.summary: In both the win and the loss, Royals and RSL players see milestones reached
articles.body:
Utah Royals FC fell 2-0 at America First Field against the Kansas City Current on Saturday evening in front of 10,809 fans, the club's second-highest attendance this season. Unable to secure the victory, the squad will now be forced to wait yet another week to officially clinch its first playoff berth in club history.

While the Royals were unable to earn the result in the battle at home, Real Salt Lake traveled to Kansas City, earning a 3-1 victory to lift itself to a second road win in the 2026 season. The victory earned the visitors an important three points to keep the push for the postseason alive in the doubleheader evening for Utah professional soccer against Sporting Kansas City.

URFC sees Del Fava and Cronin Reach key milestones in 2-0 loss

As the Utah Royals took the pitch on Saturday evening the home side was without the heartbeat of its midfield as Japanese star Mina Tanaka was out due to a hamstring injury sustained while on international duty. URFC captain Paige Cronin earned an impressive milestone Saturday against the Current, starting in her 100th NWSL match.

Iron woman Kate Del Fava returned to the pitch following her USWNT debut as a second-half substitute in Tuesday's 2-2 draw against Spain. The defensive wall not only leads the Royals in possessional passes and clearances but, made her 80th consecutive start today, the longest active streak for a single club. Del Fava has played 7,661 straight minutes, the second longest streak in club history while also having played every one of the 7,211 minutes Utah has played as a team in 79 games since the Return to Royalty in 2024.

First career brace for Guilavogui helps to lift RSL to 3-1 victory

Real Salt Lake got off to a near perfect start against Kansas City to earn just its second road win of the 2026 MLS season with goals by French attacker Morgan Guilavogui and Spanish Rookie Sergi Solans in under 15 minutes. The score by the Frenchman in the 12th minute marked his third of his first MLS season, while 2026 RSL Golden Boot leader Solans netted an impressive 12th MLS goal of his rookie season to double the visitor's lead.

The hero through the first 10 minutes of the second half was undoubtedly 22-year-old Kobi Henry who headed a ball just before it crossed the goal line in the 53rd minute following an RSL turnover that found RSL goalkeeper Rafael Cabral out of position. In the 61st minute Guilavogui found the net again for his first career RSL and MLS brace, burying a ball off a perfectly placed assist by German metronome Noel Caliskan.

"I'm not too concerned (about the remaining games) actually, I think it's just the reality of continuing to do what we've been doing. I think we showed up as the Royals we are today and almost got a result as a team that is good, a team that has scored eight or nine goals in its previous two games." — URFC Head coach Jimmy Coenraets

"I thought the guys up front did a really good job probing behind the backline, the movement behind the backline opened up a lot of space between the lines and the decisions in and around goal were really good. Our midfield of Noel and Stijn were top and then our backline of Kobi, Phil and Luc helped us be dangerous on both ends." — RSL Head coach Pablo Mastroeni

While the home side opened up the match with pressure, earning scoring chances early, it was the visiting side that struck first, heading the ball into the net off a corner kick in the 21st minute. Although the Royals surged throughout the remainder of the first half in hopes of an equalizer, the mounting calls in favor of the Current, along with a 1v1 shot against URFC 'keeper Mandy McGlynn to nearly double the lead, left the home side down 1-0 heading into the break.

As the second half began the Royals continued in its pursuit of a goal with Cece Delzer narrowly missing a header just left of the goal before recently acquired forward Jameese Joseph entered the match in the 62nd minute immediately forcing the Kansas City keeper to make two saves off powerful shots just outside the box. In the 91st minute the visitors were able to double the lead after two prior goals were disallowed due to offside. Although URFC was unable to find the back of the net the home side continued to battle with grit and energy until the final minute of the match.

The lightning-fast start for RSL put a RSL side in dire need of earning points in front with a 2-0 lead just 14 minutes into the match. The goals by Guilavogui and Solans showcased a team working as one as each score had a beautiful buildup that multiple players were involved in to seamlessly work the ball up the pitch and throughout the offensive end to lift its attackers to two early scores.

Although the visitors took an early 2-0 lead, some defensive confusion led Sporting Kansas City to earn one back in the 26th minute. After the heroics of Henry in the 53rd minute RSL was able to ease the defensive pressure with Saba Lobjanidze bringing the ball up the pitch for 2026 World Cup standout JuanMa Sanabria, whose shot from the center of the box was stopped by the SKC keeper.

The second-half goal by Guilavogui not only showcased his precise shooting abilities, but, the goal line run and slot back by Caliskan was one of beauty, helping to give RSL more breathing room, with a 3-1 lead.

Utah Royals FC remain at home next Friday, Oct. 23 to face the Seattle Reign for its final regular season match of the 2026 NWSL season. Kickoff is scheduled for 7:30 p.m. MDT with tickets available on the Utah Royals website.

Real Salt Lake will round out the weekend of home matches for Utah soccer, welcoming St. Louis City SC to the Wasatch Front on Saturday, Oct. 24, with kickoff also at 7:30 p.m. MDT and tickets for that match are also available for purchase on the RSL website.

articles.body:
Nashville SC is the first MLS club to clinch a spot in the 2027 Concacaf Champions Cup. The team has guaranteed a finish no worse than third in the league's overall standings, with matches still remaining on the 2026 schedule.

The math is simple: Nashville's position is now unreachable by any chasing club, even in a worst-case run to close out the season. That removes any dependency on other results and hands the front office an international fixture to plan around a year in advance.

Qualification doesn't end the ambition. Third place is the floor, not the ceiling, and Nashville still has reason to push for a higher finish before the playoffs begin. A stronger regular-season position carries weight heading into the postseason, where seeding and momentum matter.

The early clinch also gives the roster-building process a head start. Playing continental and domestic competitions at once demands depth — injuries, suspensions and fatigue all hit harder across a packed calendar — so locking in the Champions Cup spot now lets the front office plan accordingly instead of waiting on the regular season's final weeks.

The Concacaf Champions Cup is the region's top club competition, pitting MLS sides against teams from Mexico, Central America and the Caribbean. For Nashville, it's a chance to test the squad against different styles and raise its profile beyond the domestic league — part of a broader push by MLS clubs to build credibility on the continental stage.
